checks.name: First successful commit reports the durable sequence
Newer commit publishes its actual checkpoint bytes
Repeating a durable sequence does not write again
Older commit resolves as superseded without invoking its writer
Failed write preserves the durable sequence and previous checkpoint
A failed sequence can retry and retain the previous checkpoint backup
Concurrent writers serialize and advance in the observed order
Concurrent commit publication retains the newest file and immediate predecessor backup
A newer successful commit prevents an obsolete writer from reporting a later false failure
Invalid zero sequence cannot publish or change durable state
Successful completion observation runs after the writer lock is released
Failure releases the writer lock without publishing a durable sequence
Already-published observation releases its lock and reports no new publication
